clue.text: Originally journalistic element in specific language

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word journalistic

parts.note: argon is a chemical element, a noble gas

explanation.surface: A remark on a news writer's habit of wrapping a story in insider language.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is the specialised vocabulary of a particular trade or group.

clue.text: Pain, result of working with needle?

definitions.meaning: a sharp ache in the side, as after running
a single loop of thread made by a sewing needle

explanation.surface: Sewing all day leaves a sore side, the clue wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a sharp side ache, and a loop of thread pulled through fabric.

clue.text: Histrionics mostly in tot

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: histrionics are theatrical behaviour, drama

explanation.surface: Someone making a scene after a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits, as is a dram of whisky.

clue.text: Switched over, a new set of pots say?

indicators.note: switched means the letters of the following words are changed round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Swapping in a fresh set of pots in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovenproof dishes and casseroles form kitchen ware, an example of which is a set of pots.

clue.text: Unimportant three-in-a-bed affair?

parts.note: three people in a bed suggests the prefix tri-, meaning three
a fling is a brief romantic affair

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a romp involving three people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a tabloid 'three-in-a-bed romp'; the triple bed only signals TRI, and the affair is a FLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trifling is of little value or consequence, i.e. insignificant.

clue.text: Team of Fife partygoers includes misbehaving trio drinking hard

indicators.note: includes means the partygoers' word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: ravers are people who go to wild parties

indicators.note: drinking means the jumbled trio takes in the letter for hard
misbehaving means the letters of trio are put out of order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Scottish team's fans are revellers, three of them drunkenly unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' gives ITRO, 'drinking' makes it ITHRO, and 'includes' houses that in the partygoers. RAITH ROVERS is a football club from Kirkcaldy in Fife, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kirkcaldy football club is the best-known sports side of the Scottish county of Fife.

clue.text: Beam easily lifted

explanation.surface: A wooden beam that weighs almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a ray from a lamp and of little weight.

clue.text: Sounding like weakness, defeat

indicators.note: sounding like signals that the entry is said the same as a word for weakness

parts.note: a flaw is a weakness or defect

explanation.surface: A boxer's frailty showing as he goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in non-rhotic British speech, where the two words are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor an opponent is to knock them down, to beat or baffle them.

clue.text: Small device I'd acquire after week

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the abbreviation for week

parts.note: the contraction gives its letters without the apostrophe
to get is to acquire

explanation.surface: A shopper says they will buy a gadget after waiting a week.
explanation.definitionFit: A widget is any small gadget or mechanical contrivance whose name is unknown or unimportant.

clue.text: In various ways, when it comes to origami I'm the dude!

parts.note: dude and man are both casual forms of address for a fellow
the speaker, giving the single letter for the first person
origami is the art of folding paper

explanation.surface: A boast from an expert at Japanese paper-folding.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the boast as 'Man, I fold!': the dude speaking says folding is his thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means many and varied, in numerous different forms.

clue.text: Getting nip on front of jaw, a furry animal

indicators.note: on means the coldness word sits after the jaw word in an across entry

parts.note: the chin is the front of the lower jaw
a nip in the air is a chill

explanation.surface: An animal suffering a cold bite on its face.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a South American rodent prized for its soft dense fur.

clue.text: Function as baby carrier?

definitions.meaning: the cotangent, a trigonometric function, is abbreviated this way
a small bed with high sides that holds an infant

explanation.surface: A question about the purpose of something used for carrying an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as a verb, but it is a maths noun: the trigonometric cotangent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cot abbreviates cotangent, and a cot is a crib that holds a baby.

clue.text: Isolated individual, one sheltered by wings

indicators.note: sheltered by means the word one is placed inside the letters for the wings

parts.note: left and right, L and R, are the two wings or sides

explanation.surface: A solitary person kept safe under someone's protective wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is someone who prefers to be alone, a solitary person.

clue.text: Initially inestimable daring of legendary hero

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Praise for a mythical hero's immeasurable courage.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone hugely admired, a hero to their fans.

clue.text: After docking, side advanced

indicators.note: after means the word for side follows the word for docking

parts.note: docking a tail is cutting it
an edge is a side or border

explanation.surface: A ship's side after it has come into dock, moved forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting-edge technology is the most up to date, at the forefront of progress.

clue.text: Probable failure subordinate to setter, perhaps?

parts.note: being under someone means being subordinate to them
a setter is a breed of dog, given as an example

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler's assistant is expected to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the crossword compiler; here it is the gun-dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog in a contest is the one expected to lose.

clue.text: River in Germany, evergreen

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall in England
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A plant that keeps its leaves growing beside a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree that keeps its foliage all year.

clue.text: Slip into river

definitions.meaning: the name of rivers in Russia and in England and Scotland

explanation.surface: An instruction to slide gently into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on, and the Don is a well-known river.

clue.text: Get to the point entering data, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to narrow gradually to a tip
one who records on tape, logging information

explanation.surface: Advice to be concise while typing in information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to the point' looks like 'be brief'; it is the verb for narrowing to a tip. The second sense is someone who records onto tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle or spire tapers to a point, and someone recording onto tape is a taper.

clue.text: Twinkling beam

definitions.meaning: an instant, as in 'in a twinkling'

explanation.surface: A star's shining ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash is both a split second and a brief blaze of illumination.

clue.text: Hospital with manual worker

parts.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital
and means with, together

explanation.surface: A hospital and its labouring staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a labourer, as in farmhand or factory hand.

clue.text: Breaking horse, girl put on metal strap for it?

indicators.note: breaking means the horse word is split open to take the rest inside

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: put on means the girl word is placed after the metal word

parts.note: tin is a metal
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: Horse-breaking: a girl fitting a metal-studded strap to a young horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking horse' reads as taming a horse, but 'Breaking' is the insertion signal. 'it' in the definition points back to the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale is a strap from noseband or reins to girth that stops a horse raising its head.

clue.text: Devil put out, causing harm

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
to air an idea or programme is to put it out

explanation.surface: A demon being expelled and doing damage on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or damage it.

clue.text: Using ground to absorb energy, great idea?

indicators.note: to absorb means the scrambled letters take the energy symbol inside them
ground means crushed and reshaped, so the letters of Using are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Harnessing the earth to soak up power, a brilliant notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns USING into GNIUS, and 'to absorb' puts E inside it after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius can mean a stroke of inspired brilliance, as in 'that idea is pure genius'.

clue.text: Little sign of regret seeing predator going berserk

indicators.note: going berserk means the letters of predator run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sheds a tear on seeing a wild beast on the rampage.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tear shed is a small show of sorrow or remorse.

clue.text: Old Scot chosen to speak?

indicators.note: to speak means the entry is a word said the same as one meaning chosen

parts.note: picked means chosen

explanation.surface: An ancient Scotsman selected as the spokesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were a people of ancient northern Scotland.

clue.text: Maybe fine joke is hilarious at first

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of hilarious is used

explanation.surface: A comedian's gag starts off very funny, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, an example of a penalty, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fining someone is one way to penalise them, so it is an example of the verb.

clue.text: US state link I removed

parts.note: to connect is to link
cut means removed, as a scene cut from a film

explanation.surface: Someone explains they took out a connection to an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Connecticut is one of the New England states of the USA.
